sentences.text: ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:95890
Court No. - 47
Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 12396 of 2025

Applicant :- Shrinivas Sharma And Another
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Prabodh Dubey,Ashok Kumar Giri
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.

Hon'ble Avnish Saxena,J.
1.

Sri Arvind Prabodh Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants has moved the application under
Section 528 B.N.S.S. to assail order dated 21st September, 2024 whereby the court concerned has
taken cognizance of an offence in case crime no. 163 of 2023, P.S. Kaptanganj, District Kushinagar
against applicants simultaneously under Section 420 and 406 Ipc.
2.
The contention of learned counsel for the applicants is that two sections cannot be invoked simultaneously.
Learned counsel has also challenged the charge sheet.
3. Learned AGA has prayed for time to file counter affidavit after seeking directions.

4. Sri Dubey, has relied upon the case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and others Vs. State of U.P.
reported in 2024(10) SCC 690 on the point that two sections, viz. section 420 and 406 IPC cannot be invoked simultaneously in one incident.

sentences.text: The FIR has been registered by respondent no.2 stating therein that the applicants have fraudulently got Visa of her husband in place of Malaysia to Bangkok for providing him a job but the same was a tourist Visa to Bangkok for which the applicants have fraudulently took heavy amount from the respondent no.2 and her husband.

6. So far as, the contention of learned counsel for the applicants with regard to taking of cognizance by the trial court is concerned, the matter is squarely covered in the cited judgement but for,
quashing of entire proceeding as well as charge sheet, the contention raised by Sri Dubey that the husband of respondent no.2 has not been examined by the Investigating Officer, and there are latches in the investigation, can not be a ground to quash the charge sheet as the matter pertains to sending the husband of respondent no.2 to Bangkok on false pretext of service.
7. In the case of Delhi (supra) the Supreme Court has held that there is distinction between criminal breach of trust and cheating.

For cheating, criminal intention is necessary at the time of making of false and misleading representations, that is since inception; in criminal breach of trust, the offender is lawfully entrusted with the property and he dishonestly misappropriated the same.
In case of cheating the offender fraudulently or dishonestly induces a person by deceiving him to deliver the property.
In such a situation, both the offences cannot coexist simultaneously.
Both the offences are independent and distinct.
They are antithetical to each other, the twin provisions cannot survive with each other.
8. Hence, both the sections 406 and 420 IPC in which the Court has taken cognizance by the impugned order does not stand the test.
The bare perusal of impugned order of cognizance shows that the Court has taken cognizance in both the Sections.

9. At this juncture, Sri Dubey, learned counsel has limited his prayer to quash the cognizance order,
as the order does not reflect the application of mind, though stated that the order would be assailed in revision but he has filed an application under Section 528 B.N.S.S. with the prayer of quashing the charge sheet.

10. This Court is of the view that the point made by Sri Dubey has got substance, therefore, the impugned cognizance order dated 21st September, 2024 in which the learned Magistrate has taken the cognizance, simultaneously, under Sections 420 and 406 IPC is hereby quashed.
11. Learned Magistrate may take into consideration the case diary to pass a fresh order of cognizance.

12. In view of the above, the application is partly allowed.
Order Date :- 9.6.2025 Abhishek Sri.
(Avnish Saxena,J.)
